given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans are lent on 03-02, so they are due 03-16, and the clock is set to 03-17.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The reminders table starts empty, so no loan has a reminder before the job runs.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must hold the exact memberId, loanId and dueOn for both loans, and exactly two entries.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The `reminders` rows must have `sent_on` 2026-03-17 (today), which differs from the due date of 03-16.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so the second run meets a loan that was reminded earlier that day.
loan2 is overdue but is returned through the API before the job runs.
loan3 is due exactly on 03-17, today, which covers the boundary.

then.why: After two runs, `sent` must be exactly [loan1]. A resend, a returned loan or a not-yet-due loan would each add an entry.

given.why: `refuseFor` makes the fake refuse loan1 with a 503 reason.
B5 shows an unreachable API becomes a refused delivery. The service test only uses a refusal, and the job handles both the same way.
The job runs with overdue loans (due 03-15 and 03-16, today 03-17).

then.why: The `reminders` table must hold only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: `toContainEqual` matches the exact level, event, loanId and error text.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 is still sent after loan1 is refused. loan1 is the older, earlier-due loan, so it is probably handled first.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs over all of them.

then.why: The last log entry must equal level info, event `reminders.finished` and fields sent 2, failed 1. A wrong count, level or event fails.

given.why: A reminder with memberId, loanId and dueOn is passed straight to the client.

then.why: The recorded method must be POST and the path `/notifications`.
`objectContaining` lists only memberId and data, so changing the template to another value would still pass.
`data` must equal exactly { loanId, dueOn } by value.
The 202, 200 and 204 answers are each asserted as accepted.

then.part: any other answer ... counts as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 must give kind refused with a reason containing "400".

then.part: a failed connection counts as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error must give kind refused with a reason containing "unreachable".
